questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were different dorms I could apply to through the university. Some required an application, some did not.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I had a shared kitchen

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Don't be scared of the application proces at some of the dorms, just apply! It was my experience that it is not as competitive as dorms in Copenhagen - at least not for exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I did not hear of any exchange students that did not manage to find housing.
I stayed at Pauscollege, which I recommend. It was very close to the university, and the staff was extremely helpful.

Additional comments:
questions.answer: All the professors I experienced were very good.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses were similar to Copenhagen, however, in my experience, the work load was greater, because a 6 ECTS-point course in Leuven was somehow similar to a 15 ECTS-course in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was similar to Copenhagen, but in most classes no mandatory reading was provided. Instead, the syllabus what was the professor had said during the classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: European Taxation, Judicial Protection in the European Union, EU Company Law, EU Contract Law, Behavioral Sciences and the Law, Public International Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
First of all, I would recommend that you take a close look at what form of examination each course has. I would definitely recommend choosing at least one course where the exam is a written project, so you can hand it in before the exam period starts. If possible, choose more!

Public International Law with Professor Hernández was very interesting! It felt like an extended edition of the mandatory Public International Law in Copenhagen. The professor was very knowledgeable and enthusiastic.

EU Contract Law is also interesting. It was an intensive two-week course, which allowed me to have more flexibility the other weeks. 

Behavioral Sciences and the Law was surprisingly challenging. The exam consisted of a portfolio and five short papers, which took disproportionately much of my time

I had many overlapping classes, but it was not an issue, because some classes are recorded.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Apply for dorms through the university!
2) You have to keep up with the classes during the semester - there is not enough time to catch up in the exam period
3) Do not make your study plan too challenging. Choose some classes with a written paper exam - even if you do not find the subject interesting. It will leave you with more energy to focus on the other classes.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: KU Leuven is an amazing and well-organized university - read the emails, and everything will work out.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: If you are looking for an academic challenge, this is the place to go

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Managing the exams. It is feasible!! But required more effort than in Copenhagen
